title: Tatreez Palestinian Cross-Stitch
summary: Tatreez is the counted cross-stitch embroidery of Palestine and nearby Levantine lands, worked in red, green, gold and cream thread on dark cloth to build cypress trees, eight-pointed stars and palm stems in mirrored panels.
howToPlay: Choose a thread colour and a stitch from the strip under the cloth.
Touch a square to sew it: its twin on the other side of the centre line is sewn at the same moment, as on a real panel.
Copy the small design shown above the cloth, then press Check.
rules: Every panel is mirrored left to right, so each stitch you place is repeated on the opposite side.
A square counts only when both its stitch shape and its thread colour match the design.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Women across the villages and towns of Palestine and Lebanon have embroidered dresses, cushions and wall hangings by counting threads, with each district known for favoured colours and motifs; the craft is kept alive in homes, cooperatives and workshops.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original panels after traditional cypress, star and palm layouts)
